content.text: KÃ¶nigrufen (German: 'Calling the King') is a four-player trick-taking card game of the tarot family, played in Austria and South Tyrol. It is the most popular tarot variant in Austria and, by 2015, had become 'the favourite card game of Austrians'. The game uses a 54-card tarock pack and features a unique bidding system where players can call a king to choose a partner, along with numerous contracts and bonuses.

KÃ¶nigrufen developed in the 18th century from earlier tarot games, incorporating the bidding principle from Spanish L'Hombre and the 'calling a king' partner selection from Quadrille. The 78-card pack was stripped to 54 cards for easier handling.
Four active players (five can participate with dealer sitting out). Partners determined by calling a King or playing solo.
54-card Austrian Tarock pack: 22 trumps (Tarocks) numbered I-XXI plus SkÃ¼s, and 8 cards each in Clubs, Spades, Hearts, Diamonds.

Dealer shuffles, player to left cuts. Deal in packets of 6 cards: one to each player, one to talon (middle), repeat. Each player receives 12 cards, talon has 6. Play is anticlockwise.

items.text: Regional Scoring Variations: Different regions use different point values for contracts and bonuses. Tournament rules vary considerably.
Three-Player Variant: Each player plays for themselves with modified dealing and talon rules.
Six-Player Variant: Two teams of three players each.
Slovenian Königrufen: Played in Slovenia with modified contracts and bonuses.
